subject: Post-call exec recap: Vertex Systems - Next steps & procurement path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@vertexsystems.com>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@vertexsystems.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call exec recap: Vertex Systems - Next steps & procurement path

Hi Daniel / Sofia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick executive-level recap and proposed next steps so we can align on priorities and procurement timing: 

Key business outcomes you called out
- Reduce processing latency for customer-facing summaries from ~5s to sub-1s at peak (goal: 500ms p95)
- Cut per-token inference cost by ~40% for high-volume daytime workloads
- Improve model reliability during EMEA batch runs (avoid timeouts impacting SLAs)

Primary pain points
- Current vendor has unpredictable tail latency during peak; this is driving customer-facing errors
- Procurement/legal needs a clear SOW and SLA before exec sign-off
- Data residency requirements for EU customers are non-negotiable for several lines of business

Risks we discussed
- If we can’t commit to an SLA or EMEA residency within procurement timelines, the project will be deprioritized
- Integration effort for a PoC needs to fit within Ops team bandwidth (they requested a 2-week sandbox window)

Proposed path & owners
1) Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — I attached a draft (Vertex_Systems_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx). Proposed owner: Marissa (Redwood) / Daniel (Vertex).
2) Security/compliance checklist — Aditya to share SOC2 evidence and data-residency options (VPC + regional nodes). Target: 3 business days.
3) Pilot/PoC — 2-week sandbox with subset of traffic, Dedicated pool if needed. Laura to propose SLA language and commercial options for Dedicated vs Hosted.
4) Procurement & Legal — we’ll aim for an in-contract SLA + 60-day trial credits for exec sign-off. Proposed approver: Sofia (VP Ops).

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Aditya: share SOC2 PDF, KMS integration notes, and sample network diagram (ETA: EOD Fri).
- Marissa: update MAP with milestones & attach SLA draft (done, attached).
- Daniel/Sofia: confirm procurement timeline and any internal review dates; if you have a target sign-off date please share.

Attachment(s): Vertex_Systems_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx; Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving. Happy to set a 15-min follow-up with your procurement lead if that helps accelerate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@vertexsystems.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call exec recap: Vertex Systems - Next steps & procurement path

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying items:

- Procurement timeline: We’re looking at a finance/ops review next Thursday (2027-03-04) and an exec approver meeting the following week. If you can get the MAP and SLA in place before 03/04 that would be ideal.
- Data residency: Our EU customers must keep model inputs and logs in-region. Can you confirm if Redwood Private (VPC) supports hosting Transformer inference in eu-west-1 and whether logs can be routed to our customer-managed S3?
- Credits: Sofia — any flexibility on the trial length? Our legal prefers 30-60 days.

Happy to jump on a short call with Aditya if needed to go over the security docs.

—Daniel
VP, Platform Engineering
Vertex Systems

Hi Daniel / Sofia — looping in our procurement and solutions teams. Quick answers to your questions and proposed phrasing for the MAP/SLA to streamline internal reviews:

1) EU data residency: Redwood Private can be deployed into eu-west-1 and we can configure log routing to a customer-managed S3 bucket behind your KMS. Aditya, I’ve asked you to include the runbook and one-page network diagram in the SOC packet.

2) Trial credits & duration: We can offer a 45-day trial for the PoC, with up to $50k in credits for the pilot (covers Dedicated burst capacity). If you need 60 days we can escalate to Director of Sales for approval; Marissa will coordinate.

3) SLA ask: For procurement ease, suggested language is provided in Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf. High-level: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools, latency SLOs for p95 under agreed load, and a credit schedule for breaches. If your legal team has redlines, please share; we’ll aim to turn them around within 3 business days.

Escalation items for execs to be aware of:
- If timeline slips past 03/04, we risk missing your Q2 integration window and this will push production launch beyond your internal milestone.
- Data residency verification for EU customers is prioritized; we'll commit to an audit run during the PoC.

I’ve attached the SLA draft and updated MAP with milestone owners. Marissa — I left a note in the MAP about finance approver contact details.

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
